full_judgment:
3. The case of the defendant is. that on 22.6.95. the plaintiff-petitioner got a couple of tickets to participate in Monsoon Ball night of the club held in the premises of it But instead of bringing his wife. he entered into the Ball room with a local unknown lady. Security Guard since failed to identify her and thinking that she would be his wife allowed the plaintiff-petitioner to enter into the ball room along with the said lady. Some time after it attracted the notice of other members of the club when they started whispering. The lady then fled away. On the following day the security guard filed a petition against the petitioner before the Secretary of the club. The Secretary brought the matter before the Executive Committee and on discussion the Executive Committee served a notice on 27.6.95 upon the petitioner to show cause as to why necessary action should not be taken against him for violation of the club rules. On 17.7.95. the petitioner submitted a reply. The disciplinary committee being dissatisfied over the reply and as to the language of the same also on 18.7.95 asked the petitioner to appear before the disciplinary committee. On 20.7.95 the petitioner appeared and he was examined by the committee. Before the disciplinary committee the petitioner refused that he had brought any local lady guest with him. Again it was brought before the executive committee on 23.7.95. The committee unanimously decided that the conduct of the petitioner would endanger the stability and harmony of the club and accordingly they served a letter under Article 25 of the Memorandum of Articles of Association of the club asking the petitioner to resign. The petitioner did not resign within 24 hours as was stipulated time. The executive committee then expelled him from the roll of the members of the club and hence the suit. The suit is pending before the trial Court. 

 4. In the suit an application was filed for temporary injunction with a prayer that till disposal of the suit the petitioner should not be disturbed from taking part in the different functions and activities of the club. Against his prayer for temporary injunction the Dhaka Club as defendant submitted a written objection. On hearing both the parties the trial Court granted temporary injunction. Against the said order of temporary injunction passed by the trial Court Dhaka Club took Misc. Appeal 253 of 1995. The plaintiff petitioner contested the appeal which was allowed and the trial Court order was set aside. Against the same the present revision has been preferred by the plaintiff-petitioner. 

 7. Mr. Shafique Ahmed, the learned Advocate for the petitioner, submits that the action taken against the petitioner expelling him is mala fide and in utter violation of the provision of article 34 wherein, according to him, a Member can be suspended for any action if it is proved to endanger the stability and harmony of the club or if it is prejudicial to the interest of the club. According to the learned Counsel, the petitioner has not done anything bringing his activity as alleged within the ambit of disciplinary action which has been taken against him and Mr. Ahmed submits that the club could suspend his membership at best for a period not exceeding 3 months. So the expulsion of a permanent member is mala fide and apparently illegal. Therefore, according to him, the appellate Court has acted illegally, resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice. Mr. Ahmed submits that if injunction is not granted the petitioner will be seriously prejudiced and suffer an irreparable loss and he will be looked down in the circle of his friends and before other members of the club. He further submits that the allegation has not been proved against the delinquent plaintiff petitioner who claims prima facie case and balance of convenience and inconvenience in his favour. 

 8. On the other hand, Mr. Habibul Islam Bhuiyan, the learned Counsel for the Dhaka Club, submits that the allegation against the petitioner is very serious because in violation of the club rules, he brought a local lady on the aforesaid date and moreover, the petitioner has used unpalatable and in disciplinary language in his reply submitted on 27th June 1995 which shows audacity of the mind of the delinquent as a member of the club. Mr. Bhuiyan also submits that the action is not illegal, mala fide and uncalled for one. According to him, the provision of article 35 of the Memorandum of Articles provides that if after a proceeding under article 34 in the opinion of the executive committee it is essential in the interest of the club that any member should cease to be a member they may call upon him to resign within a specific date and if the member fails to resign the executive committee may expel him forthwith. The learned Advocate also submits that the club authorities observed all the legal formalities before taking the action against the petitioner. Therefore, according to him, there is nothing mala fide or illegal having been done by the club authority against the petitioner. Mr. Bhuiyan also submits that temporary injunction if granted it will tantamount to interference with the internal affairs and administration of the club which is a private company and that the petitioner has no prima facie case and balance of convenience and inconvenience is not in favour of the petitioner. 

 "In the instant case two general principles are involved. The courts will not normally interfere with the internal management of a company. Secondly, the court generally will not interfere with the decision of the domestic tribunal. Any order of injunction whether ad-interim or temporary is to be passed keeping in view above two principles of law, lastly, before an injunction is granted it is necessary to see what is that balance of convenience and inconvenience Whether the balance of convenience and inconvenience would be in favour of the plaintiff or the defendant. Since these questions are involved in the instant matter, we do not like to interfere with the impugned order passed by the learned District Judge." 

 The provision of section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure has been amended lastly by Ordinance No JCL VIII of 1983. This court is only to see whether failure of justice has been caused by the impugned order from perusal of the judgment and order of the appellate Court. I find that although it has passed the impugned judgment in a very slipshod manner but as I see he has considered the prima facie case and balance of convenience and inconvenience in an implied manner because it is very critical to decide the same, as it may invite comment upon the merits of the suit itself at this stage when the suit in pending. In the case of the Secretary Dhaka Club Ltd. vs. Mustafa Jamal 31 DLR 387, the former Chief Justice Mr. Shahabuddin Ahmed has expressed his view that the decision of the lower court should not be interfered with during the pendency of the suit itself. 

 11. I am not at all inclined to indulge on the question of merits on the points involved in the principal litigation. As in my view it will invoke infringement on the right of the parties to get fair and final decision from the trial Court by adducing evidence. Regard being and to the facts and circumstances of the case for me purpose of a decision only in the matter of temporary injunction, I find prima facie case and balance of convenience and inconvenience in favour of the defendant opposite party, Dhaka Club.
